abel-beth-maachah.title: Abel-beth-maachah
abel-beth-maachah.note: A fortified city in the far north near Dan. Its own people called it a mother in Israel, which is how you said a town led the region. Joab besieged it to get at the rebel Sheba, and it was taken later by Ben-hadad when Asa paid him to attack, then by Tiglath-pileser.

abi-2.title: Abi
abi-2.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abi-2.note: Hezekiah's mother and Ahaz's wife, named as the daughter of a Zechariah. Chronicles calls her Abijah instead.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

achbor.title: Achbor
achbor.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
achbor.note: A royal official under Josiah. He is one of the men sent to the prophetess Huldah after the law scroll turned up in the temple.

adaiah-4.title: Adaiah
adaiah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

adrammelech.title: Adrammelech
adrammelech.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
adrammelech.note: A son of Sennacherib who killed his own father. The same name belongs to an Assyrian god the people of Sepharim sacrificed their children to after they were resettled in Samaria.

adrammelech-2.title: Adrammelech
adrammelech-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
adrammelech-2.note: 2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

ahab.title: Ahab
ahab.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahab.note: King of northern Israel for about twenty-two years. He married Jezebel, a Phoenician princess. She brought Baal worship into a kingdom that was supposed to belong to Yahweh alone, and he let her.

ahaz.title: Ahaz
ahaz.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahaz.note: He abandoned his predecessors' reforms, sacrificed his own son in the fire and closed the temple. Facing a coalition of enemies, he paid Assyria for protection instead of trusting the promise Isaiah brought, and Judah stayed an Assyrian vassal for a generation. The Immanuel prophecy was given in his crisis.

ahaziah.title: Ahaziah
ahaziah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahaziah.note: Ahab's grandson through his mother Athaliah, and king of Judah for only one year. He was killed in the same purge that brought Jehu to power.

ahaziah-2.title: Ahaziah
ahaziah-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahaziah-2.note: He ruled northern Israel, fell through a palace lattice, and sent to a foreign god to ask about healing. Elijah rebuked him for not asking the Lord.

ahijah.title: Ahijah
ahijah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahijah.note: One of 8 men called Ahijah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named 4 times in 1 Kings and 2 Kings.

ahikam.title: Ahikam
ahikam.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahikam.note: A court official under Josiah. He backed the warnings of Huldah the prophetess and later protected Jeremiah from a mob that wanted him killed, and Gedaliah was his son.

amana.title: Amana
amana.note: Two things share the name. At 2 Kings 5:12 the Hebrew margin reads Amana for the Abana, the river of Damascus Naaman preferred to Israel's water. In the Song of Solomon it is a mountain, likely the southern summit of the Anti-Lebanon range, where the Abana rises.

amaziah.title: Amaziah
amaziah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amaziah.note: He took Judah's throne after his father Joash was assassinated and executed the killers but spared their children, as the law said. Then he beat Edom, brought its idols home and worshipped them. A war he picked with northern Israel ended with him captured and Jerusalem's walls torn down.

amittai.title: Amittai
amittai.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amittai.note: Jonah's father, from Gath-hepher in Galilee. Nothing else is recorded of him.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amon.title: Amon
amon.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amon.note: The son of Manasseh. He followed his father's early idolatry and never turned back, and his own officials killed him after two years. The people executed the plotters and made his young son Josiah king.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

amoz.title: Amoz
amoz.about: Isaiah's father living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amoz.note: Isaiah's father, and not the prophet Amos: the names look alike in English but come from different Hebrew names entirely.

anammelech.title: Anammelech
anammelech.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
anammelech.note: A god of the people of Sepharvaim, whom the Assyrians resettled in Samaria after deporting the northern kingdom in 722 BC. The colonists burned their children in the fire to Anammelech and to Adrammelech beside it.

aphek-3.title: Aphek
aphek-3.note: 2 Kings names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

ararat.title: Ararat
ararat.note: Noah's ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat as the floodwaters went down. The region is in what is now eastern Turkey.

argob-2.title: Argob
argob-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
argob-2.note: 2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

arieh.title: Arieh
arieh.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
arieh.note: He died with King Pekahiah of Israel when the officer Pekah murdered the king in the citadel of the palace at Samaria. He and Argob are named only as victims of the coup.

arnon.title: Arnon
arnon.note: A swift river running into the Dead Sea from the east, the line between Amorite and later Moabite land and Israel's tribes beyond the Jordan. Its gorge still carries water in the Wadi al-Mujib. King Mesha of Moab's inscription, the Moabite Stone, boasts of building a highway across it.

aroer.title: Aroer
aroer.note: A border town on the edge of Moabite and Ammonite territory. It marked the southern limit of the land Israel took east of the Jordan.

arpad.title: Arpad
arpad.note: A Syrian city near Hamath. Assyrian kings kept naming it to show what they could conquer, and it fell to Tiglath-pileser III after a long siege around 740 BC. Its ruins are at Tell Rifaat, north of Aleppo.

asaiah.title: Asaiah
asaiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaiah.note: One of the officials Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah.

asaph-2.title: Asaph
asaph-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaph-2.note: Not David's singer. This Asaph is the one in 2 Kings 18:18 and Isaiah 36:3, and nothing else about him is recorded here.

ashima.title: Ashima
ashima.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
ashima.note: A god, not a person: the god of the people of Hamath, whom the Assyrians resettled in Samaria after deporting the northern kingdom. Little is known of the cult beyond this one notice.

ashtoreth.title: Ashtoreth
ashtoreth.about: A female deity in the Old Testament
ashtoreth.note: A Canaanite and Phoenician goddess of fertility and war, closely tied to Baal worship. Solomon built her a shrine late in his reign to please a foreign wife, and that is given as a main reason the kingdom split.

asshur.title: Asshur
asshur.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
asshur.note: Shem's son, whose name stuck to the land and empire of Assyria on the upper Tigris. Assyria became the great power of the eighth and seventh centuries BC, deported Israel's northern tribes after Samaria fell, and kept threatening Judah.

athaliah.title: Athaliah
athaliah.about: Queen living at the time of Divided Monarchy
athaliah.note: Ahab and Jezebel's daughter, married into Judah's royal house. When her son Ahaziah was killed she took the throne and murdered nearly the whole royal family, the only woman to rule Judah in her own name. Six years later the priest Jehoiada brought out the infant Joash, who had survived, and she was executed.

ava.title: Ava
ava.note: Also Ivah, a city in Mesopotamia from which the Assyrians sent settlers to fill Samaria after 722 BC. Sennacherib's field commander later named Ava's conquered gods, with those of Hamath and Sepharvaim, to push Hezekiah into surrender.

avims.title: Avims
avims.note: The Avvim lived in villages around Gaza before the Caphtorim, from Crete, drove them out. 2 Kings 17:31 gives the same name to settlers from Avva placed in Samaria by the Assyrians.

azaliah.title: Azaliah
azaliah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azaliah.note: Shaphan's father. Shaphan was the royal scribe who read the newly found Book of the Law to King Josiah.

azariah.title: Azariah
azariah.about: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah.note: This is King Uzziah of Judah under his other name.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

baal-shalisha.title: Baal-shalisha
baal-shalisha.note: A man from here brought Elisha twenty barley loaves and some fresh grain, and the prophet fed a hundred people with it. The place was in the district of Shalisha, apparently not far from Gilgal.

baal-zebub.title: Baal-zebub
baal-zebub.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
baal-zebub.note: Lord of the flies, the Philistine god of Ekron. King Ahaziah of Israel sent messengers to ask him about his health. Elijah confronted it by asking whether Israel had no God of its own.

baasha.title: Baasha
baasha.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
baasha.note: He killed Nadab, Israel's second king, and wiped out the rest of Jeroboam's family to take the northern throne. That fulfilled a prophecy against Jeroboam's line. Baasha's own violence brought the same kind of end on his house.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

baladan.title: Baladan
baladan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
baladan.note: His son was the Babylonian king who sent envoys to Hezekiah after his illness. About Baladan himself nothing else is recorded.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

benhadad-2.title: Benhadad
benhadad-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
benhadad-2.note: A later king of Aram-Damascus under the same dynastic name, in 2 Kings 13. Amos 1:4 names him too.

benhadad-3.title: Benhadad
benhadad-3.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
benhadad-3.note: His siege of Samaria starved the city until Elisha predicted a sudden turn. He is the Ben-hadad of 2 Kings 6 and 8.

berodach-baladan.title: Berodach-baladan
berodach-baladan.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
berodach-baladan.note: Merodach-baladan under another spelling. He was the Chaldean king who twice took the throne of Babylon from Assyrian control in the late eighth century BC, and in 2 Kings 20:12 he sends envoys to Hezekiah.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-gilgal.title: Beth-gilgal
beth-gilgal.note: It is probably the Gilgal near Jericho where Israel first camped, and it sent singers to the dedication of Jerusalem's rebuilt walls under Nehemiah.

beth-shemesh.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh.note: It was a Levitical city on Judah's northern border, its name meaning house of the sun. When the Philistines sent the ark back, it came here first and was welcomed with sacrifice.

bidkar.title: Bidkar
bidkar.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
bidkar.note: He had ridden with Jehu as a chariot officer under Ahab. When Jehu killed King Jehoram of Israel, he told Bidkar to throw the body into the field that had been Naboth's.

bozcath.title: Bozcath
bozcath.note: A town in the Shephelah of Judah near Lachish and Eglon. Adaiah came from there. His daughter Jedidah was the mother of King Josiah.

careah.title: Careah
careah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
careah.note: Johanan's father. Johanan was the commander who warned Gedaliah of the plot to kill him after Jerusalem fell, and Careah is named each time his son is.

carmel.title: Carmel
carmel.note: Elijah's contest with the prophets of Baal happened on this mountain ridge on Israel's Mediterranean coast. Fire came down from heaven when Elijah prayed, and Baal had nothing to answer with.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

chemosh.title: Chemosh
chemosh.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
chemosh.note: Moab's national god. Solomon built him a shrine to please one of his foreign wives, and that is among the reasons given for the enemies God raised against Solomon late in his reign.

chush.title: Chush
chush.note: Cush as a land. It lay south of Egypt, roughly modern Sudan and Ethiopia, and the Old Testament keeps coming back to it as a distant, exotic country.

cuth.title: Cuth
cuth.note: The Assyrians conquered the northern kingdom and moved people from this Babylonian city into Samaria, and they brought their god Nergal with them. It is identified with Tell Ibrahim northeast of Babylon. Later Jews used Cuthites, often as an insult, for Samaritans.

damascus.title: Damascus
damascus.note: A city has stood here, on a fertile plain watered by the Barada northwest of Mount Hermon, since before the patriarchs. It was the Aramean capital that fought Israel through the ninth and eighth centuries BC. Saul was converted on the road into it, and the street called Straight was a real colonnaded street whose columns have been found.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

eden-2.title: Eden
eden-2.note: A region in northern Mesopotamia, not the garden. It sold richly worked cloth to Tyre, and the Rabshakeh named it outside Jerusalem among lands Assyria had already taken. Many identify it with Bit-Adini on the middle Euphrates, which Shalmaneser III annexed.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

edomite.title: Edomite
edomite.note: Esau's descendants, living in Seir south and east of the Dead Sea. Kin to Israel and at odds with it for most of the record. Egyptian texts mention Edom as early as the thirteenth century BC, and its capital Busayra and the copper works at Khirbat en Nahas have both been excavated.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

ekron.title: Ekron
ekron.note: Northernmost of the five Philistine cities, given to Judah and then Dan but never firmly held. The ark's last stop before the Philistines sent it back. Ahaziah of Israel sent there to ask Baal-zebub about his health, and an inscription at Tel Miqne naming Ikausu, or Achish, son of Padi settles the site.

elah-2.title: Elah
elah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elah-2.note: Father of Hoshea, Israel's last king before Assyria's conquest. Each time Hoshea is introduced, Elah's name comes with him.

elath.title: Elath
elath.note: A port on the Gulf of Aqaba near Ezion-geber. Solomon held it, Edom took it back, Uzziah recovered it for Judah, and Syria finally got it. Modern Eilat keeps the name.

eliakim.title: Eliakim
eliakim.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliakim.note: Hezekiah's palace administrator, sent with the other officials to talk to the Rabshakeh while Sennacherib had Jerusalem under siege. Another Eliakim was the king Necho renamed Jehoiakim.

elijah.title: Elijah
elijah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elijah.note: A prophet from Tishbe in Gilead who took on Ahab and Jezebel over Baal worship and beat 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel with fire from heaven. Straight after, he ran into the wilderness sure he was the last faithful man left, and God met him in a quiet voice, not in wind or earthquake or fire. He did not die; a whirlwind took him up while Elisha watched.

elisha.title: Elisha
elisha.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elisha.note: A farmer's son who was ploughing when Elijah threw his cloak over him. He left the oxen, followed, and asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit when the older man was taken up. His miracles run from poisoned water made clean to Naaman healed of leprosy, and a dead man thrown into his tomb came back to life when he touched the bones.

elishama-4.title: Elishama
elishama-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elishama-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice across 2 Kings and Jeremiah.

elnathan-2.title: Elnathan
elnathan-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elnathan-2.note: 2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

esar-haddon.title: Esar-haddon
esar-haddon.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
esar-haddon.note: Sennacherib was murdered and Esarhaddon took the Assyrian throne after him. He carried Manasseh of Judah off to Babylon, and his own inscriptions list Manasseh among the vassal kings paying him tribute.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

evil-merodach.title: Evil-merodach
evil-merodach.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
evil-merodach.note: Nebuchadnezzar's son, Amel-Marduk in Babylonian records. In his first year he let Jehoiachin out of prison and gave him a seat at the royal table for life. He lasted only about two years before he was overthrown.

gaba.title: Gaba
gaba.note: Another English spelling of Geba, a Levitical city in Benjamin by the pass of Michmash. Jonathan raided a Philistine garrison there, and later it marked the line between the northern and southern kingdoms.

gadi.title: Gadi
gadi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
gadi.note: Only ever named as the father of Menahem, who killed Shallum, took the throne of Israel and ruled brutally.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gath-kephr.title: Gath-kephr
gath-kephr.note: Jonah was born here, in Zebulun's territory, though the town is better known as Gath-hepher. Local tradition puts his tomb in the village of Mashhad by a hill called Nebi Yunus, near Nazareth.

gedaliah.title: Gedaliah
gedaliah.about: Governor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
gedaliah.note: After Jerusalem fell, Babylon made him governor of Judah over the poor left in the land, and he told them to settle down and submit. Ishmael, of the royal line, murdered him within months, and the rest fled to Egypt in spite of Jeremiah telling them not to go.

gehazi.title: Gehazi
gehazi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
gehazi.note: Elisha's servant. When Elisha turned down Naaman's payment, Gehazi ran after the general and lied his way into silver and clothes, and Elisha, who knew without being there, gave him Naaman's leprosy for good.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gileadite.title: Gileadite
gileadite.note: Someone from Gilead, east of the Jordan, or of the clan named after Machir's son. Jephthah is the best known, the judge who beat the Ammonites and made the rash vow about his daughter.

gilgal-2.title: Gilgal
gilgal-2.note: Named once, in 2 Kings, and nowhere else.

gozan.title: Gozan
gozan.note: When Assyria took the northern kingdom, it resettled Israelite captives in this region of northern Mesopotamia.

gur.title: Gur
gur.note: Jehu's servants caught King Ahaziah of Judah on the ascent of Gur, near Ibleam, as he ran, and wounded him fatally.

habor.title: Habor
habor.note: After Samaria fell in 722 BC, the Assyrians deported the northern kingdom's people to this river and its district. It is the Khabur, a big tributary of the Euphrates in what is now northeastern Syria.

halah.title: Halah
halah.note: A district in Assyria, probably near Nineveh, where Israelites were deported after Samaria fell. Sargon II boasts in his own inscriptions of taking tens of thousands from Samaria around 722 BC.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hamutal.title: Hamutal
hamutal.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hamutal.note: She was one of Josiah's wives, and two kings of Judah were her sons, Jehoahaz and Zedekiah, who both reigned after Josiah died.

haran.title: Haran
haran.note: Abraham's family stopped and settled here for a while on the way toward Canaan, and Abraham set out again from Haran in Genesis 12:4. The city was likely named after his brother.

harhas.title: Harhas
harhas.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
harhas.note: Grandfather of Shallum, the keeper of the king's wardrobe. Shallum's wife was Huldah the prophetess, the one consulted when the book of the law turned up in Josiah's temple repairs. Chronicles spells him Hasrah.

haruz.title: Haruz
haruz.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
haruz.note: He came from Jotbah, and his daughter Meshullemeth married King Manasseh of Judah and bore King Amon. That one notice is all.

hazael.title: Hazael
hazael.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hazael.note: Elijah was told to anoint him king of Aram, and the prophet wept over what Hazael would do to Israel. He smothered his own king to get the throne and was one of Israel's worst enemies for decades. An inscription with his name has been found in Damascus.

hazor.title: Hazor
hazor.note: The head of all the Canaanite kingdoms, in Joshua's words, and the biggest city-state in the region. Its fall decided the northern campaign. The dig there found a huge Bronze Age city to match.

hena.title: Hena
hena.note: The Assyrian messenger names it to Hezekiah as one more city Assyria has already taken. It is usually identified with Anah on the Euphrates, near Sepharvaim.

hephzi-bah.title: Hephzi-bah
hephzi-bah.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hephzi-bah.note: My delight is in her. She was Hezekiah's wife and Manasseh's mother. Isaiah takes the same name for Jerusalem restored, no longer the abandoned wife.

hezekiah.title: Hezekiah
hezekiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hezekiah.note: One of Judah's few good kings. He came after Ahaz, reopened the temple, tore down the high places, and broke up the bronze serpent Moses had made once people began worshipping it. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem in 701 BC, Hezekiah prayed, Isaiah promised deliverance, and the siege broke overnight. His seal impression has been dug up near the Temple Mount, and his tunnel still runs under the city.

hillkiah.title: Hillkiah
hillkiah.about: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hillkiah.note: The high priest under Josiah who found a forgotten scroll of the law while the temple was being repaired. What he found set off Judah's last great reform.

hillkiah-2.title: Hillkiah
hillkiah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hillkiah-2.note: Known through his son, the palace official who went out to meet the enemy's envoys at the wall, in 2 Kings 18 and again in Isaiah 36. Nothing else is recorded about him.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hosea.title: Hosea
hosea.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hosea.note: God told Hosea to marry Gomer, a woman who would be unfaithful, and his taking her back again and again became his book's picture of God with Israel. He prophesied to the north in the decades before it fell to Assyria. The same name, spelled Hoshea, belongs to four other men.

huldah.title: Huldah
huldah.about: Prophetess living at the time of Divided Monarchy
huldah.note: Josiah's officials took the scroll found in the temple to her, a prophetess in Jerusalem, and not to any of the men prophesying at the time. She told them it was genuine. Judgment was coming on Judah, she said, though not in Josiah's lifetime.

ibleam.title: Ibleam
ibleam.note: A town given to Manasseh inside Issachar's borders, where the Canaanites were never driven out. King Ahaziah of Judah took his death wound near there, running from Jehu. It is generally identified with Khirbet Bel'ameh, near Jenin.

ijon.title: Ijon
ijon.note: In Naphtali, in Israel's far north. Ben-hadad took it at Asa's request, and later Tiglath-pileser III took it in Pekah's reign, a conquest his own inscriptions also list. It is usually identified with Tell Dibbin.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

isaiah.title: Isaiah
isaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
isaiah.note: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.

ishmael.title: Ishmael
ishmael.about: Jeremiah's adversary living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ishmael.note: After Jerusalem fell this Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, the governor the Babylonians had set over the land, and the killing sent another wave of Jews running for Egypt.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jaazaniah.title: Jaazaniah
jaazaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jaazaniah.note: More than one man had the name. One is an army captain who came to the new governor after Jerusalem fell, in Kings and again in Jeremiah; another heads the family Jeremiah brought into the temple and offered wine.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

janoah.title: Janoah
janoah.note: Named once, in 2 Kings, and nowhere else.

jecholiah.title: Jecholiah
jecholiah.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jecholiah.note: Amaziah's wife and Uzziah's mother, a woman of Jerusalem. Her son came to the throne at sixteen and reigned over fifty years. Nothing further is recorded of her.

jedidah.title: Jedidah
jedidah.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jedidah.note: Amon's wife, and mother of Josiah, the king who reformed Judah more thoroughly than almost anyone.

jehoaddan.title: Jehoaddan
jehoaddan.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoaddan.note: Jehoash's wife, and Amaziah's mother. She came from Jerusalem, and the record gives her the brief notice most queen mothers of Judah get.

jehoahaz.title: Jehoahaz
jehoahaz.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoahaz.note: King of northern Israel, and a weak one, worn down by Aramean pressure through his reign.

jehoahaz-2.title: Jehoahaz
jehoahaz-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoahaz-2.note: Josiah's son. He reigned in Judah three months before Pharaoh Necho deposed him and took him to Egypt, where he died.

jehoash.title: Jehoash
jehoash.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoash.note: Joash under a longer spelling: the king of Judah hidden from Athaliah as a child.

jehoash-2.title: Jehoash
jehoash-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoash-2.note: The king of Israel who beat the Arameans and then beat Amaziah, king of Judah. Jehoash is the longer form of Joash.

jehoiachin.title: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiachin.note: Three months on Judah's throne, then he surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar and went to Babylon with much of Jerusalem's upper class. He spent thirty-seven years a prisoner. A new Babylonian king let him out and fed him at the royal table for the rest of his life, and 2 Kings ends there.

jehoiada.title: Jehoiada
jehoiada.about: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiada.note: After Athaliah killed the royal family, this priest hid the baby Joash in the temple for six years and then led the coup that put him on the throne. While Jehoiada lived, Joash ruled well. They buried him among the kings.

jehoiakim.title: Jehoiakim
jehoiakim.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiakim.note: Pharaoh Necho put him on Judah's throne. When Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, he cut it off a section at a time and burned it in the fire pot, while his advisors begged him to stop. Jeremiah had it written out again, with more added.

jehonadab.title: Jehonadab
jehonadab.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehonadab.note: Rechab's son, who gave his family rules against wine and fixed houses, and they kept them for generations. He rode with Jehu to watch the purge of Baal worship.

jehoram.title: Jehoram
jehoram.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoram.note: Two kings had the name. One was Ahab's son in Israel, killed by Jehu; the other ruled Judah, killed his brothers, married Ahab's daughter Athaliah and brought Baal worship south, and died of the long illness Elijah had foretold.

jehoshaphat.title: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoshaphat.note: A king of Judah who sent officials and Levites through the land to teach the law. His alliance with Israel kept going wrong, and in one battle enemy soldiers took him for Ahab and nearly killed him. When Moab, Ammon and Edom invaded together, he sent singers ahead of the army, and the invaders destroyed each other.

jehoshaphat-3.title: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoshaphat-3.note: One of 4 men called Jehoshaphat. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in 2 Kings.

jehosheba.title: Jehosheba
jehosheba.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehosheba.note: She was King Jehoram's daughter. When Athaliah killed the royal family after Ahaziah's death, Jehosheba hid the infant Joash in the temple for six years, and Chronicles says she was the high priest Jehoiada's wife.

jehoshua-4.title: Jehoshua
jehoshua-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoshua-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Kings is the only book that names him.

jehozabad.title: Jehozabad
jehozabad.about: Moabite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehozabad.note: One of the two servants who killed King Joash of Judah. Chronicles gives his mother as a Moabite woman.

jehu.title: Jehu
jehu.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehu.note: Anointed king by one of Elisha's students with a single job, to wipe out Ahab's family, and he did it thoroughly: Joram, Jezebel, every descendant left, then Baal's priests tricked into one building and killed together. The Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III shows an Israelite bowing and paying tribute, named as Jehu, though whether the figure is the king himself or his envoy is argued either way.

jeremiah-3.title: Jeremiah
jeremiah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeremiah-3.note: The prophet's namesake, and nothing more to him than a daughter: she was mother to two kings of Judah, and he is named only as her father.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jeroboam-2.title: Jeroboam
jeroboam-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeroboam-2.note: Jeroboam the second, king of Israel generations after the first Jeroboam. His reign was a time of unusual prosperity and military success for the north.

jeroboam.title: Jeroboam
jeroboam.about: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
jeroboam.note: Solomon's official who led the ten northern tribes out after Rehoboam refused to lighten the labour his father had laid on them. To stop his people going back to Jerusalem to worship, he set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan with a priesthood of his own. Every northern king after him gets measured against that sin.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jerusha.title: Jerusha
jerusha.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jerusha.note: She was Zadok's daughter, wife of King Uzziah and mother of Jotham, who reigned after him, and nothing more is recorded of her.

jezebel.title: Jezebel
jezebel.about: Queen living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jezebel.note: A princess of Sidon, married to Ahab to seal an alliance. As queen she pushed Baal worship and hunted down Yahweh's prophets, and when Naboth would not sell his vineyard she had him framed and stoned. Elijah said dogs would eat her. When Jehu came, she did her makeup and her hair and met him at a window, and he had her thrown down.

jezreel.title: Jezreel
jezreel.note: A valley and town in northern Israel. Naboth's vineyard was there, the one Ahab and Jezebel stole, and it was there that Jehu wiped out Ahab's whole house. Hosea named one of his children Jezreel to say judgment was coming.

jezreelite.title: Jezreelite
jezreelite.note: Someone from Jezreel. The one everybody knows is Naboth, the vineyard owner Ahab and Jezebel had falsely accused and killed so they could take his land, and Elijah went straight at them for it.

joah.title: Joah
joah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joah.note: The royal recorder, sent out with the other officials to talk to the Rabshakeh when Sennacherib's army sat outside Jerusalem.

joash.title: Joash
joash.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joash.note: Seven years old when he was made king of Judah, after six years hidden in the temple from his grandmother Athaliah, who had killed the rest of the royal family. While Jehoiada the priest lived, Joash ruled well and repaired the temple. Afterwards he let it go, and when Jehoiada's son stood up to him he had the man stoned in the temple court. His own murder followed.

joash-2.title: Joash
joash-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joash-2.note: A king of the north, and not the boy king of Judah who shares his name. He went down to weep over a dying prophet, and later he beat the king of Judah in battle when that king picked a fight with him.

johanan.title: Johanan
johanan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
johanan.note: He commanded troops after Jerusalem fell and warned Gedaliah, the new governor, that someone was coming to kill him. Gedaliah would not believe it, and the plot went through.

jonah.title: Jonah
jonah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jonah.note: God told him to preach to Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, Israel's enemy, and he took a ship the other way. A storm, three days in a great fish, and then he did preach, and the whole city repented and God spared it. That made Jonah furious. The book stops with God questioning his anger and leaves it there.

joram.title: Joram
joram.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joram.note: Another form of Jehoram, and the kings of Israel and Judah called by it are covered under that entry.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

josiah.title: Josiah
josiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josiah.note: Made king of Judah at eight after his father Amon was murdered. In his eighteenth year workmen repairing the temple found a forgotten scroll of the law, and its reading set off Judah's last great reform: pagan altars torn down, the priests of the high places killed, and a Passover like none since the judges. He died young at Megiddo, trying to stop the Egyptian army reaching Assyria.

jotbah.title: Jotbah
jotbah.note: Meshullemeth came from there, King Manasseh's wife and mother of Amon. Where it was has been lost. It is a different place from Jotbathah in the wilderness.

jotham.title: Jotham
jotham.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jotham.note: He carried on his father Uzziah's steady rule in Judah, building up Jerusalem's defences and bringing the Ammonites under, and Scripture counts him one of the few kings who did right in the Lord's eyes. The high places stayed, though.

jozachar.title: Jozachar
jozachar.about: Ammonite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jozachar.note: One of two court officials who killed King Joash of Judah at Beth-millo. Chronicles says it was revenge for the priest Zechariah, and calls him Zabad.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kedesh.title: Kedesh
kedesh.note: A city of refuge in Galilee, one of six where someone who had killed by accident could run and be safe. Barak came from there, the commander Deborah called up.

kidron.title: Kidron
kidron.note: The valley along Jerusalem's east side, between the city and the Mount of Olives. Reforming kings dumped smashed idols and temple rubbish into it, and Jesus crossed it with his disciples on the way to Gethsemane the night he was arrested.

kir-haraseth.title: Kir-haraseth
kir-haraseth.note: Moab's fortress capital, modern Kerak in Jordan. When Mesha of Moab rebelled after Ahab died, Israel, Judah and Edom besieged him there, and he sacrificed his own son on the wall, which ended the siege. His own account of the revolt survives on the Moabite Stone, found in 1868.

lachish.title: Lachish
lachish.note: A heavily fortified Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands. Joshua took it, Rehoboam rebuilt it into one of Judah's strongest fortresses, and in 701 BC Sennacherib's Assyrians took it again. Assyria carved the siege on wall reliefs now in the British Museum. The ruins at Tell ed-Duweir also gave up the Lachish Letters, written during Babylon's last siege, just before Jerusalem fell.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

libnah.title: Libnah
libnah.note: A royal Canaanite city near Lachish that Joshua took and gave to the Levites in Judah. It held out against Sennacherib's Assyrians. Hamutal, Josiah's wife and mother of two of Judah's last kings, came from there.

maachathite.title: Maachathite
maachathite.note: Someone from Maacah, the small Aramean kingdom near Mount Hermon that Israel never fully brought under. Eliphelet, one of David's officers, was a Maachathite.

madai.title: Madai
madai.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
madai.note: Japheth's son, and the ancestor of the Medes, who later joined Persia in taking Babylon.

malcham.title: Malcham
malcham.note: The national god of the Ammonites, also called Milcom. Solomon went after him in his old age, and the high place built for him stood near Jerusalem until a later king tore it down.

manasseh-2.title: Manasseh
manasseh-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
manasseh-2.note: Hezekiah's son, who reigned in Judah longer than any king and did more harm than any. He rebuilt the high places, practiced sorcery, apparently sacrificed his own son, and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. Chronicles says captivity in Babylon broke his pride and he repented, but his reforms died with him.

mattan.title: Mattan
mattan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mattan.note: A priest of Baal, killed at his own altar when the people of Jerusalem tore Baal's worship down after Queen Athaliah was overthrown.

mattaniah.title: Mattaniah
mattaniah.about: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
mattaniah.note: Zedekiah's name before Nebuchadnezzar made him king and changed it.

megiddo.title: Megiddo
megiddo.note: It guarded the pass into the Jezreel Valley. A Canaanite royal city, it went to Manasseh and Solomon rebuilt it as a chariot city. Deborah and Barak beat Sisera on its plain, and King Josiah died there facing Pharaoh Necho, a death mourned so deeply it became proverbial. Thutmose III's siege of it around 1457 BC is carved in detail on the walls of Karnak.

menahem.title: Menahem
menahem.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
menahem.note: He took the throne of northern Israel by murdering the king before him, then savagely sacked a city that would not open to him. To keep his crown he paid a huge tribute to Tiglath-pileser the Third, and Assyrian inscriptions name Menahem paying it.

mesha-3.title: Mesha
mesha-3.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mesha-3.note: The king of Moab who paid Israel heavy tribute until Ahab died, then broke away. With the armies of Israel, Judah and Edom about to overrun him, he sacrificed his own son on the city wall to Chemosh. His own account of the revolt survives on the Moabite Stone, found at Dibon in 1868, and it names the "house of Omri."

meshullam-10.title: Meshullam
meshullam-10.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
meshullam-10.note: One of 20 men called Meshullam. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Kings.

meshullemeth.title: Meshullemeth
meshullemeth.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
meshullemeth.note: King Manasseh's wife and the mother of King Amon. She was the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah, and it is rare for the record to say where a queen mother of Judah came from.

micaiah-2.title: Micaiah
micaiah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
micaiah-2.note: 2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

molech.title: Molech
molech.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
molech.note: A god of the Canaanites and Ammonites, worshipped with the sacrifice of children. The law forbids it again and again, and still some kings did it, Ahaz and Manasseh among them.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

naaman.title: Naaman
naaman.about: Syrian living at the time of Divided Monarchy
naaman.note: Commander of the Aramean army, a great man, and a leper. A captured Israelite girl told his household about a prophet in Samaria. Elisha did not even come out, only sent word to wash seven times in the Jordan, and Naaman almost went home angry before his servants talked him round. He came out of the water clean, and Gehazi, who ran after him for a payment, got his leprosy.

naboth.title: Naboth
naboth.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
naboth.note: His vineyard sat next to King Ahab's palace, and he would not sell it, because Israel's law kept family land in the family. Jezebel had false witnesses accuse him of blasphemy, he was stoned, and Ahab took the vineyard. Elijah met Ahab there and announced the end of his dynasty.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nathanmelech.title: Nathanmelech
nathanmelech.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nathanmelech.note: An official in Josiah's time. The horses earlier kings had dedicated to the sun stood near his room at the temple entrance, and Josiah took them away.

nebat.title: Nebat
nebat.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
nebat.note: Jeroboam's father, and he is only ever named in "Jeroboam son of Nebat," the phrase the books of Kings use again and again for the king blamed for making idol worship the habit of the north.

nebuchadnezzar.title: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebuchadnezzar.note: King of Babylon. He destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off, and the Bible still calls him the tool God used to judge his people. Daniel tells how, after boasting of his greatness, he went mad and lived like an animal for seven years, until he gave God the glory and got his throne back.

nebuzaradan.title: Nebuzaradan
nebuzaradan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebuzaradan.note: He commanded the Babylonians who burned Jerusalem and its temple. To Jeremiah, though, he showed unusual kindness, and let the prophet choose whether to go to Babylon or stay in Judah.

necho.title: Necho
necho.about: Pharaoh living at the time of Divided Monarchy
necho.note: Necho the Second, pharaoh of Egypt, killed King Josiah at Megiddo. Afterwards he removed Josiah's son Jehoahaz and set up another son, Jehoiakim, under him.

nehushta.title: Nehushta
nehushta.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nehushta.note: Elnathan's daughter, from Jerusalem. She was King Jehoiakim's wife and the mother of Jehoiachin, who reigned three months at eighteen before Nebuchadnezzar took him, and she was carried to Babylon with him in 597 BC. The Babylonian Chronicle records that capture of Jerusalem.

nehushtan.title: Nehushtan
nehushtan.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
nehushtan.note: Hezekiah's scornful name for the bronze serpent Moses had made in the wilderness. People had taken to burning incense to it, so Hezekiah broke it up, calling it a mere piece of bronze.

nergal.title: Nergal
nergal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
nergal.note: A Mesopotamian god of war, plague and the underworld, worshipped at Cuthah. When Assyria moved people from Cuthah into Samaria after 722 BC, they brought him with them.

nethaniah.title: Nethaniah
nethaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nethaniah.note: Father of Ishmael, the man of royal blood who murdered Gedaliah, the governor Babylon set over Judah after Jerusalem fell.

netophathite.title: Netophathite
netophathite.note: From Netophah, a small town near Bethlehem. Several of David's mighty men carried the name, and later some Levitical singers did too.

nibhaz.title: Nibhaz
nibhaz.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
nibhaz.note: An idol the Avite settlers brought to Samaria when the Assyrians moved them there. Old tradition says it was shaped like a dog.

nimshi.title: Nimshi
nimshi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nimshi.note: Jehu's grandfather, who survives almost entirely inside the phrase "Jehu son of Nimshi."

nineveh.title: Nineveh
nineveh.note: The capital of the Assyrian empire. Jonah preached there against his will and watched the city repent, and Nahum later announced its destruction once it had gone back to its old cruelty.

nisroch.title: Nisroch
nisroch.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
nisroch.note: Sennacherib, king of Assyria, was killed by his own sons in the temple of Nisroch, an Assyrian god and not a man at all.

omri.title: Omri
omri.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
omri.note: An army commander who took the northern throne after a civil war. He founded a dynasty. Assyrian records went on calling Israel the House of Omri long after he was dead.

parbar.title: Parbar
parbar.note: It is a place on the temple grounds, not a person, on the west side, probably a colonnade or open court. Gatekeepers were posted there.

pedaiah-3.title: Pedaiah
pedaiah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
pedaiah-3.note: 2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

pekah.title: Pekah
pekah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
pekah.note: He took the northern throne by murdering the king before him. Then he joined Syria against Assyria, invaded Judah, and tried to force King Ahaz into the alliance.

pekahiah.title: Pekahiah
pekahiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
pekahiah.note: King of northern Israel for two years, until his own officer Pekah killed him and took the throne.

pharaoh.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: The king Moses stood in front of. God sent Moses to him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and he hardened his heart through plague after plague before he let them go.

pharaoh-5.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-5.note: In the divided-kingdom years this was the Egypt people were tempted to lean on, mocked as a broken reed that pierces the hand of whoever leans on it, and Isaiah warned against going down to Pharaoh for help.

pharpar.title: Pharpar
pharpar.note: It was one of the rivers of Damascus, with the Abana. Naaman did not see why he should wash in the Jordan when those were right there. It is usually identified with the Nahr al-Awaj.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

pul.title: Pul
pul.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
pul.note: Another Old Testament name for the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser the Third, the one Menahem of Israel paid off to keep his own throne.

rab-saris-2.title: Rab-saris
rab-saris-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rab-saris-2.note: 2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

rabshakeh.title: Rabshakeh
rabshakeh.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rabshakeh.note: A title, not a name: a senior Assyrian officer. During Sennacherib's siege he stood outside Jerusalem's walls and taunted the people in Hebrew, trying to break them over the heads of their leaders.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

ramoth-gilead.title: Ramoth-gilead
ramoth-gilead.note: A city of refuge in Gad's land east of the Jordan, and too useful for Israel and Aram to leave alone. Ahab died after being wounded there trying to take it back with Jehoshaphat.

rechab.title: Rechab
rechab.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rechab.note: His son Jehonadab laid down a rule his descendants kept for generations: no wine, no permanent houses. Jeremiah held the Rechabites up as a rebuke to Judah.

remaliah.title: Remaliah
remaliah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
remaliah.note: Pekah's father. Isaiah keeps calling Pekah "the son of Remaliah," and it is not meant kindly.

remmon-6.title: Remmon
remmon-6.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
remmon-6.note: 2 Kings names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

rezeph.title: Rezeph
rezeph.note: Sennacherib's field commander named it as proof that no god had saved anyone from Assyria. Usually identified with Rasappa.

rezin.title: Rezin
rezin.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rezin.note: King of Aram-Damascus. He and Pekah of Israel came against Judah together, and Ahaz panicked and turned to Assyria instead of trusting Isaiah's word that the threat would pass.

riblah.title: Riblah
riblah.note: Twice a wartime headquarters. The town sat on the east bank of the Orontes in the land of Hamath, where the roads between Egypt, Palestine and Babylon crossed. Pharaoh Necho used it first, and later Babylon did the same.

rumah.title: Rumah
rumah.note: Named once, in 2 Kings, and nowhere else.

samaria.title: Samaria
samaria.note: Omri bought a hill from a man called Shemer and built a capital on it. Samaria took over from Tirzah as the seat of the northern kingdom. Ahab and the kings after him ruled from there.

samaritans.title: Samaritans
samaritans.note: Settlers from Babylon, Cuthah and other places, brought in after Assyria deported most of the northern kingdom in 722 BC.

sela.title: Sela
sela.note: Named once, in 2 Kings, and nowhere else.

sennacherib.title: Sennacherib
sennacherib.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
sennacherib.note: He besieged Jerusalem in Hezekiah's reign and boasted in his own inscriptions that he shut Hezekiah up like a bird in a cage. He never claims he took the city.

sepharvaim.title: Sepharvaim
sepharvaim.note: A city the Assyrians took. They moved its people into Samaria after deporting Israel, and they became part of the mix that later made up the Samaritans.

sepharvite.title: Sepharvite
sepharvite.note: People from Sepharvaim, settled in Samaria by the Assyrians. 2 Kings 17:31 says they burned their children as offerings to their gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.

seraiah.title: Seraiah
seraiah.about: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
seraiah.note: The chief priest in Jerusalem when it fell. Nebuchadnezzar had him executed, and the name runs on through several later generations of priests.

seraiah-4.title: Seraiah
seraiah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
seraiah-4.note: One of 8 men called Seraiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in 2 Kings and Jeremiah.

shallum-2.title: Shallum
shallum-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shallum-2.note: He killed the king of Israel and took the throne himself, then was killed in turn after one month.

shallum-5.title: Shallum
shallum-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shallum-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice across 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

shalmaneser.title: Shalmaneser
shalmaneser.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shalmaneser.note: King of Assyria from about 727 to 722 BC. When Hoshea of Israel held back tribute and looked to Egypt, Shalmaneser came and laid siege to Samaria.

shaphat.title: Shaphat
shaphat.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shaphat.note: Elisha's father, and when Elijah found Elisha out ploughing he was still known as the son of Shaphat.

sharezer.title: Sharezer
sharezer.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
sharezer.note: He and his brother Adrammelech killed their own father, Sennacherib, king of Assyria. Both 2 Kings and Isaiah record it in a line.

shebna.title: Shebna
shebna.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shebna.note: He ran Hezekiah's palace. He was also carving himself a grand tomb, and Isaiah told him he would be thrown out of office and die in a foreign land. Eliakim would take his place.

shimath.title: Shimath
shimath.note: An Ammonite woman. Her son Jehozabad and another man killed King Joash of Judah in his bed, reportedly in revenge for the prophet Zechariah.

shomer-2.title: Shomer
shomer-2.about: Moabite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shomer-2.note: A Moabite woman, the mother of Jehozabad, one of the royal servants who killed King Joash of Judah. She is also called Shimrith.

shunamite.title: Shunamite
shunamite.note: Someone from Shunem, a village in Issachar. Abishag, brought in to look after David in his old age, was one. So was the woman who took in Elisha and saw her son raised.

shunem.title: Shunem
shunem.note: A village of Issachar near Jezreel. The Philistines camped here before the battle on Mount Gilboa where Saul and his sons died, and a woman here built a room for Elisha.

silla.title: Silla
silla.note: King Joash of Judah was killed by his own servants at a place called Silla, somewhere in or near Jerusalem on a road going down. Nobody is sure where.

so.title: So
so.about: Pharaoh living at the time of Divided Monarchy
so.note: King Hoshea of Israel stopped paying tribute to Assyria and sent to So, an Egyptian king, for help. That move brought on the invasion that ended with the fall of Samaria.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

succothbenoth.title: Succothbenoth
succothbenoth.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
succothbenoth.note: A god the settlers from Babylon brought with them to Samaria, after the Assyrians conquered the northern kingdom.

sur.title: Sur
sur.note: One of the gates in Jerusalem where the guard was posted on the day Jehoiada made the young Joash king and removed Athaliah. The account in 2 Chronicles 23:5 calls it the gate of the foundation instead.

syrian.title: Syrian
syrian.note: The Arameans, the people around Damascus, mostly in the wars of the kings in 2 Kings.

tanhumeth.title: Tanhumeth
tanhumeth.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tanhumeth.note: A Netophathite whose son Seraiah was one of the army captains who came over to Gedaliah after Jerusalem fell.

tartak.title: Tartak
tartak.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
tartak.note: One of two gods the Avvites worshipped after the Assyrians resettled them in Samaria. The other was Nibhaz, and nothing else is known about this one.

tartan.title: Tartan
tartan.note: An Assyrian title, roughly commander-in-chief, not a man's name. One tartan came with the delegation demanding Jerusalem's surrender from Hezekiah, and an earlier one took Ashdod for Sargon.

telassar.title: Telassar
telassar.note: The Assyrian king's messenger names it with Gozan and Haran, places already conquered. The children of Eden lived there, somewhere in Mesopotamia.

tiglath-pileser.title: Tiglath-pileser
tiglath-pileser.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tiglath-pileser.note: He was the third Assyrian king of the name, and he took territory from Israel and Syria and collected tribute. His own inscriptions record the same campaigns and payments 2 Kings describes.

tikvah.title: Tikvah
tikvah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tikvah.note: His son Shallum was married to Huldah, the prophetess who was asked about the law scroll found in Josiah's temple repairs.

tipsah-2.title: Tipsah
tipsah-2.note: Menahem took this town and treated it savagely. The other Tipsah is the Euphrates crossing at the far edge of Solomon's reach.

tirhakah.title: Tirhakah
tirhakah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tirhakah.note: The Kushite pharaoh of Egypt in the early seventh century BC, known in his own records as Taharqa. Word that he was marching against Assyria made Sennacherib send Hezekiah a threatening letter during the siege of Jerusalem.

tirzah.title: Tirzah
tirzah.note: An old Canaanite royal city that served as capital of the northern kingdom before Samaria was built. The Song of Solomon sets its beauty beside Jerusalem's. Menahem seized the throne from there.

tishbite.title: Tishbite
tishbite.note: Elijah is always the Tishbite, the man from Tishbe. Where Tishbe was, in Gilead or further north in Galilee, depends on how you read the Hebrew of 1 Kings 17:1.

tophet.title: Tophet
tophet.note: The place in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned to Molech, until Josiah defiled it. Jeremiah said the valley would fill with the dead. Later Jewish pictures of Gehenna drew on it.

uriah-2.title: Uriah
uriah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
uriah-2.note: A priest, not the Hittite. 2 Kings 16 has him at work in the temple, and Isaiah 8:2 calls him as a witness.

uzza.title: Uzza
uzza.note: Uzzah put his hand out to steady the ark when the oxen stumbled, and he died on the spot. David was afraid, and the ark stayed where it was for three months before it went on to Jerusalem.

uzziah.title: Uzziah
uzziah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
uzziah.note: King of Judah at sixteen, he reigned fifty-two years and rebuilt the army and the economy. Then he went into the temple to burn incense himself, which no king was allowed to do. The priests confronted him and leprosy broke out on his forehead while he stood there.

zachariah-3.title: Zachariah
zachariah-3.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zachariah-3.note: A king of Israel in the divided-kingdom years, in 2 Kings 14:29 and 15:8–11.

zachariah-4.title: Zachariah
zachariah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zachariah-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice across 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

zadok-3.title: Zadok
zadok-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zadok-3.note: One of 7 men called Zadok. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

zair.title: Zair
zair.note: Joram of Judah broke out through an Edomite army that had him surrounded here, when Edom revolted. It was east of the Dead Sea, exact spot unknown.

zebudah.title: Zebudah
zebudah.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zebudah.note: Josiah's wife and the mother of Jehoiakim, who took the throne after his brother Jehoahaz's short reign.

zedekiah.title: Zedekiah
zedekiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zedekiah.note: The last king of Judah. Nebuchadnezzar put him on the throne, and he rebelled anyway, against everything Jeremiah told him. Jerusalem was destroyed, he was caught running, his sons were killed in front of him, and then they blinded him.

zephaniah.title: Zephaniah
zephaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zephaniah.note: A priest, not the prophet of the book. Jeremiah's verses show him carrying messages between the king and Jeremiah, and 2 Kings 25:18 counts him among those taken when Jerusalem fell.

zibiah.title: Zibiah
zibiah.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zibiah.note: She was from Beersheba, and she was the mother of King Joash of Judah, the boy hidden from Athaliah and crowned at seven.

zimri.title: Zimri
zimri.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zimri.note: He killed King Elah of Israel and took the throne, and lasted seven days. The army made its own commander king, and Zimri burned the palace down over himself rather than be taken.

zion.title: Zion
zion.note: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.
